Police subjected eight hijras to forced nudity and public presentation after arrest, while people with disabilities protesting for higher allowances were attacked and the allowance was not increased despite commitments.","notes":["The excerpt supports the fewer-than-1-percent statistic but does not include the 51-percent child-marriage figure."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E011","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The Election Commission was criticized for weak independence; some 2023 local elections showed improved performance because opposition and independent candidates won, but observer accreditation raised concerns about expertise and AL links. The BNP's political space narrowed after it adopted strikes and blockades; more than 20,000 members were reportedly imprisoned and at least eight died in custody. Women faced social and political barriers, while religious, ethnic, and other marginalized groups remained underrepresented and LGBT+ people faced limitations on political participation.","notes":["The excerpt supports political barriers and underrepresentation for specified groups, but not the unqualified claim that women and LGBT+ people remained underrepresented."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0001-E014","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The AL's abolition of the caretaker-election system in 2011 was followed by continued AL rule; the 2018 election involved allegations of vote rigging and reprisals. In 2023, Hasina resisted calls to hold the 2024 election under a caretaker government, while she faced allegations of misusing state institutions to repress opponents and influence the election.","notes":["The excerpt attributes the allegations to Hasina's situation but does not specify that opposition parties made them."]}]}
